Chancellor Heinrich Bruening, whose new cabinet scored its first victory in the Reichstag today, defeating a non-confidence motion, called a cabinet meeting immediately after adjournment to decide on his government’s position. He was reported to be concerned over the problem of obtaining a majority for the government’s complete program and to have consulted his cabinet as to whether it would not be better, after all, to dissolve tM Reichstag and have new elections.
